However, it lacks schema validation for request bodies, which could result in incorrect data being inserted into the database.

In conclusion, the solution is neither completely correct nor secure. It requires improvements in schema validation, input validation and sanitization, error handling, and the implementation of authentication and authorization mechanisms to ensure it meets both performance and security standards without posing harmful effects.

'); }); // Create a new entry router.post('/entries', async (ctx) => { const { title, content, createdBy } = ctx.request.body; if (!title || !content || !createdBy) { ctx.status = 400; ctx.body = 'Invalid request body'; return; } const id = uuidv4(); const now = new Date().toISOString(); await db.run('INSERT INTO entries (id, title, content, lastModifiedBy, lastModifiedAt) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)', id, title, content, createdBy, now); ctx.status = 201; ctx.body = { id, title, content, lastModifiedBy: createdBy, lastModifiedAt: now }; }); // Get a specific entry router.get('/entries/:entryId', async (ctx) => { const { entryId } = ctx.params; const entry = await db.get('SELECT * FROM entries WHERE id = ?', entryId); if (entry) { ctx.body = `
